findings.title: Octopus Issues Notification on Information Security Incident
findings.summary_md: Octopus's 27 November notice says it detected abnormal activity from a cyberattack that morning and immediately took containment measures. It reports names and photographs for approximately 7,500 customers, with some records also involving Automatic Add Value Service bank codes and top-up amounts, plus contact details for approximately 22,000 merchants. The company says no credit-card or bank-account information was affected, core services remained normal, and affected customers would be contacted directly by email or SMS.

findings.title: Octopus says cyberattack affected about 7,500 customers’ personal data
findings.summary_md: Newsdesk reported Octopus's 27 November disclosure that names and photographs for about 7,500 customers and contact details for about 22,000 merchants were affected. It says some records may include auto top-up bank codes and amounts, while credit-card and bank-account information was not involved and no customer financial loss had been found. The report says core services remained normal, with only a small number of functions potentially affected by preventive measures.

findings.title: Personal data of 7,500 Octopus users leaked
findings.summary_md: RTHK reported that Octopus detected abnormal activity on Friday morning and that no customer financial loss had been identified. The report says exposed customer data included names and photographs, while some Automatic Add Value Service users had bank codes and top-up amounts accessed; about 22,000 merchants had contact names, titles, email addresses and phone numbers compromised. Octopus said core services continued normally and a small number of features might be temporarily affected.

findings.title: Octopus cyberattack exposes data of 7,500 customers and 22,000 merchants
findings.summary_md: The Standard reported that Octopus took immediate containment measures after detecting the intrusion on Friday morning. It says customer records included names and photographs and, in some cases, Automatic Add Value Service bank codes and top-up amounts, while merchant exposure was limited to business contact details. The report says no credit-card numbers or bank-account details were leaked, no customer financial losses had been reported, and card and wallet balances remained protected.
